sources.title: Paula Doumani Dupuy, Bronze Age Central Asia (2016)
sources.note: Relevant full-text chapter sections read through Oxford CDN. Northern Central Asia periodization, ceramics and conclusion distinguish varied communities and changing scientific chronologies.

sources.title: Irina P. Panyushkina and colleagues, Calendar Age of Lisakovsky Timbers (2008)
sources.note: Direct publisher PDF read, especially printed pp. 460-462 and 467-468. Distinguish raw calibrated timber ages from authors' adjusted cemetery chronology.

sources.title: Peter W. Jia and colleagues, Adunqiaolu: new evidence for the Andronovo in Xinjiang, China (2017)
sources.note: Publisher abstract and indexed author-hosted ResearchGate article checked: pp. 626-628 house plan and extensions; pp. 632-636 radiocarbon and interpretation. No generic family-size inference.

sources.title: Seasonal movements of Bronze Age transhumant pastoralists in western Xinjiang (2020)
sources.note: Full primary study accessible also as PMC7641598. Sections 4.3, 5.1.1 and conclusion. Modern herding observations are analogies, while ancient dung gives independent support.

sources.title: New evidence for supplementary crop production, foddering and fuel use by Bronze Age transhumant pastoralists in the Tianshan Mountains (2021)
sources.note: Full primary text read. Site description, Seeds, Chronology and Subsistence strategies. Barley directly dated late seventeenth through thirteenth centuries BCE; associated millet not independently AMS dated.

sources.title: Alicia Ventresca Miller and colleagues, Dental health, diet, and social transformations in the Bronze Age (2014)
sources.note: Direct primary paper PDF checked, original DOI 10.1016/j.quaint.2014.01.036. Abstract, methods pp. 7-8, discussion and conclusion pp. 15-16. 77 individuals and 1,173 teeth concern both sites together.

sources.title: Paula N. Doumani and Michael D. Frachetti, Bronze Age textile evidence in ceramic impressions (2012)
sources.note: Institutional abstract read; DOI 10.1017/S0003598X00062827. Indexed original figure 5 dates Begash sample 10 to 1650-1000 BCE. This is a regional sequence with later material, not one narrowly dated Andronovo costume.

sources.title: M. M. Savenkova, Textile Decoration and Patterns on the Andronovo Vessels: Possible Reconstructions (2018)
sources.note: Institute of Archaeology and Ethnography publisher abstract read. Experimental tablet weaving supports a hypothesis about design transfer; does not establish a recovered loom or alphabet.

sources.title: National Museum of the Republic of Kazakhstan, Exhibition activity
sources.note: Institutional exhibition account, Archaeology Hall, paragraphs on Bronze Age metallurgy and sites Atasu, Myrzhik, Taldysai, Kalba and Narym. Broad Bronze Age context, not dates for each artifact.

sources.title: Rasmus G. Bjørn, Indo-European loanwords and exchange in Bronze Age Central and East Asia (2022)
sources.note: Full scholarly article read, abstract, introduction, Table 1 and Indo-Iranic discussion. Identifies linguistic silence and proposes comparative loanword models; these are not inscriptions. Author and date verified from PMC metadata.

proposedOverrides.name: Andronovo
proposedOverrides.summary: Varied Bronze Age steppe communities, craft networks and households, with regional chronologies beyond the map cutoff.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One new detailed archaeological-horizon card; no associations with Sintashta, Afanasevo or later Scythian records.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: One broad Polygon in hb/borders/world-bc2000.json, bbox [50.29306224278588,37.388482470726956,95.51771774637368,55.45327919207368]. Distribution envelope is not a political border or evidence of continuous occupation.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Atlas interval retained as approximate map coverage. Adunqiaolu/Begash later samples explicitly dated in public prose. Regional nomenclature and phase boundaries vary by scholar.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: No securely identified contemporary inscription reproduced; comparative linguistic reconstructions are not presented as attested samples.
